Bug_Title: EC: Invocation of equals() on an array, which is equivalent to == (EC_BAD_ARRAY_COMPARE)
Bug_Details:
This method invokes the .equals(Object o) method on an array. Since arrays do not override the equals
method of Object, calling equals on an array is the same as comparing their addresses. To compare the
contents of the arrays, use java.util.Arrays.equals(Object[], Object[]).
To compare the addresses of the arrays, it would be
less confusing to explicitly check pointer equality using ==.
 java.util.Arrays.equals(Object[], Object[]) ==
Bug_Explanation: The bug occurs because the equals method is called on an array object. In Java, arrays do not override the equals method from Object, so calling equals on arrays compares their memory addresses rather than their contents. This can lead to unexpected results when checking if two arrays contain the same elements.
Trigger_Explanation: The test cases trigger the bug by using the showBug method to compare arrays that have identical contents but different memory addresses. The .equals method is used incorrectly, leading to false results in array content comparison.
